newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T shares rebound in active trade.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T shares rebound in active trade.

text.p: B.A.T Industries Plc shares rose in active trade on Monday after positive press and analyst comment on the stock and amid continued talk of a settlement in U.S. tobacco lawsuits, dealers said.

A report in the Times newspaper said B.A.T was under pressure to bring forward a demerger of its tobacco and financial services operations, while analysts at Schroders raised their valuation on the stock, dealers said.
No-one at B.A.T was immediately available for comment.
Analysts at Schroders were also not immediately available for comment, though market sources said the brokerage had put a valuation of between 670p and 830p on the stock.
Separately the Financial Times Lex column on Saturday said the market was in effect valuing B.A.T's 600 million stg U.S. profits at zero.

"Assume B.A.T agrees to give away 50 percent of those profits to settle all (U.S. lawsuits)," the paper said. "If the other 50 percent was then given a more normal rating, it would add around 12.5 billion or 15 percent to its market value."
Rebounding from its sharp decline over the past week, the stock was up 12-1/2p at 506-1/2 by 1008 GMT in active trade of 5.7 million shares, making it the most active stock in the FTSE 100 index.

The Sunday Telegraph newspaper said B.A.T had proposed a $3 billion fighting fund across the industry to cushion against rising legal costs, while a report in the Times said B.A.T was believed to have decided that a demerger could take place by the end of the year.
No-one from the company was immediately available for comment.
B.A.T on Friday dismissed a decision by rival Ligett Group to settle U.S. tobacco litigation, saying the move would not force it to seek a similar pact.
However, chief executive Martin Broughton said at the time of the company's results earlier this month it could be time to explore ways of settling the claims because of the mounting costs.
